subject: Split ledger remit plan & conditional credit line
messages:
From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finoptics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Delroy <marcus.delroy@finoptics.com>, procurement@finoptics.com
Date: Fri, 28 Aug 2026 17:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Net60 + VAT handling for new usage tier

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the detailed onboarding call earlier this week. We’re finalizing procurement for the new usage tier (estimated $180k ARR) and have a standard payment policy of Net60 for software vendors. Before we issue a PO, procurement and finance asked whether Redwood can accept Net60 for the first 3 invoices and then move to Net45 thereafter.

Two compliance notes from our side:
- We need a short credit buffer (either a $25k retainer or an escrow arrangement) because we’re onboarding into multiple EU subsidiaries and VAT reconciliation is manual on our end.
- We’ll share VAT registration scans this afternoon, but we typically require a tax clause that specifies who is responsible for VAT adjustments post-invoice.

Can you confirm if Redwood can:
1) Accept Net60 for the first 3 invoices (then Net45),
2) Accept a split remittance (60% at invoice, 40% at Net30) as an alternative, or
3) Provide a conditional credit line tied to us providing the VAT docs and a one-time security deposit?

Attaching our standard PO terms for reference (not attached here).

Best,
Susan
Procurement Manager
FinOptics


From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finoptics.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Net60 + VAT handling for new usage tier

Hi Susan —

Appreciate the clear ask and the context. Short answer: we can be flexible but need a firm guardrail so Redwood’s cash and tax exposure are covered while the accounts are brought online. Below is a pragmatic set of options; happy to pick one that fits FinOptics’ internal approvals.

Option A — Conditional credit line (preferred):
- Redwood issues a conditional credit line up to $80k after we receive VAT registrations and a signed credit addendum.
- Credit line is backed by a one-time refundable security deposit of $25k or an escrow agreement.
- Invoices issued Net45; first 3 invoices may be Net60 if deposit is in place.

Option B — Split-ledger remit (fast execution):
- Each invoice: 60% due on invoice date, remaining 40% due Net30.
- No deposit required but we run a quarterly review for spend and may require an on-demand hold if delinquency exceeds 30 days.

Option C — Short-term Net60 with ramp and cap:
- Net60 for first 3 invoices, capped at $50k total receivable under Net60.
- Post ramp move to Net30/45 depending on payment behavior.

On VAT: we ask that FinOptics confirm which entity will be billed for EU usage. If billing is to an EU subsidiary, we will invoice net of VAT where you provide valid VAT IDs; otherwise Redwood will invoice with VAT and you may issue credit notes for adjustments. We’ll attach a simple tax clause in the credit addendum.

Attachments: Redwood_Credit_Terms_v1.pdf (credit addendum template), payment-schedule-proposal.xlsx (Option B sample).

If you can confirm which option you prefer by Monday, we’ll assign a finance rep and aim to get the addendum signed within 3 business days.

Thanks —
Kimberly Park
Head of Commercial Finance | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com

From: Susan Lee <susan.lee@finoptics.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: Marcus Delroy <marcus.delroy@finoptics.com>, procurement@finoptics.com
Date: Sun, 30 Aug 2026 01:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: Net60 + VAT handling for new usage tier

Thanks Kimberly — quick internal check with Marcus and legal. Two follow-ups:
1) Given our internal PO cadence, Option B (split-ledger remit) looks easiest operationally, but we want the split to be 50/50 (to align with our cash distribution) rather than 60/40. Can Redwood accept 50% immediate and 50% Net30?
2) We will provide VAT IDs for the EU entities by EOD Monday. If Redwood can accept a 50/50 split without the $25k deposit, we’ll proceed to issue the PO and include the signed quote.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Susan

> Thanks Kimberly — quick internal check with Marcus and legal. Two follow-ups:
> 1) Given our internal PO cadence, Option B (split-ledger remit) looks easiest operationally, but we want the split to be 50/50 (to align with our cash distribution) rather than 60/40. Can Redwood accept 50% immediate and 50% Net30?
> 2) We will provide VAT IDs for the EU entities by EOD Monday. If Redwood can accept a 50/50 split without the $25k deposit, we’ll proceed to issue the PO and include the signed quote.

Hi Susan — thanks for the clarity. We can accept a 50/50 split under these conditions: 
- Redwood requires a rolling credit review after the first two invoices (30 days post-invoice). If both invoices are paid on time, we’ll waive the deposit requirement going forward.
- If an invoice becomes >45 days overdue, Redwood reserves the right to suspend new provisioning for that account until balances are current.
- VAT IDs must be provided for all billed entities before we process EU-tax-exempt invoices; otherwise tax will be applied to the invoice and credit notes handled after reconciliation.

Marissa (CS lead) and Aditya (sales) — looped to confirm operational handoffs: Marissa to confirm provisioning timeline if 50/50 accepted; Aditya to confirm quoting/PO acceptance path.

If that works, please send the signed PO and VAT docs and we’ll send a final one-page credit addendum to sign.

Best,
Kimberly
